eilean_guide.text: Welcome to Eilean Donan, where three sea lochs meet. It is named after St Donnán, who is said to have lived here about AD 600.
The castle dates from the 13th century. In 1719 government warships bombarded it during a Jacobite rising, and it lay in ruins for about 200 years.
Lt Col John MacRae-Gilstrap rebuilt it between 1912 and 1932. The footbridge you walked across is quite modern, but do not tell the ghosts.
